message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a fully built pink monopoly. I am cash poor against the dark blues of p1, who dropped out of this auction. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 is the only remaining bidder with cash and a light blue monopoly. The current bid is $37, so the minimum next bid is $38. I will cap my bid around $150 to deny p4 the Pennsylvania-Avenue pair. Neither p4 nor p1 can complete a green set without me.

A green monopoly requires Pacific, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania Avenue. p1 owns the mortgaged Pacific, so p4 cannot complete the set even if they win NC. I will bid to secure two of three greens for trading leverage.

Bidding under $150 would let me mortgage North Carolina immediately and net $112 in cash. This creates positive expected value if I can use that liquidity before my next roll.

p1 has only $29 and dark blues built. They might trade Pacific to p4 for cash, completing a green monopoly. No houses remain in the bank, so no one can build more. I will not hotel my pink monopoly. From Pennsylvania Avenue, a roll of 3 lands on Park Place, which p1 owns with 3 houses and charges $1100.

A roll of 5 on Park Place would cost $1700, which is fatal. A roll of 12 on Oriental costs $400, which I can afford. I will bid $38 to keep the auction open and deny p4 a cheap steal.

I will bid up to the mortgage value of $150. If I win and mortgage immediately, I net about $1 in cash plus blocking value. If p4 wins at $149, they only gain $1 from mortgaging, not a gift. I am also weighing whether owning North Carolina is worthwhile at all.

I am now calculating the cash impact of owning North Carolina. Unimproved rent is only $26, so mortgaging it would block the green pair but cost me immediate cash. Selling all twelve pink houses would raise about $600, giving me roughly $1326 total. That covers the $1100 rent on Park Place, yet Boardwalk at $1700 remains fatal even fully liquidated.

Owning North Carolina unmortgaged would raise total cash to about $1476, still short of Boardwalk's $1700. Mortgaging it immediately after purchase nets $838, which is better liquidity than not buying at all. I am unsure whether the game rules allow mortgaging a property right after winning an auction.

I realized I cannot mortgage a property during the auction decision itself. The action state only offers bid or drop.

Even if I bid $38, selling all twelve pink houses would raise about $600, giving me roughly $1288 total. That still covers the $1100 rent on Park Place. At a $150 bid, cash would be $576 plus $600, totaling $1176, which also covers it.

The immediate cash cost of bidding is therefore manageable. I will proceed with the auction.

A bid of roughly $226 is the hard ceiling for Park Place survival. The $150 cap is therefore safe. I will keep raising to $38 and drop if p4 exceeds about $150. p4 has $763 but sits in jail, so they may continue bidding for the green pair.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a bid for North Carolina Avenue in the auction.

I have $726 and one Get Out of Jail Free card. The auction is at $41 with p4 as the high bidder. I will bid $42 to win under the $150 mortgage value. This nets cash and blocks p4 from a PA+NC pair.

Mortgaging immediately after purchase yields $108 cash back, making this a clear profit. I am now weighing the risks.

Cash drops to $684 after the bid. I can mortgage North Carolina immediately upon acquisition, before my next roll. The worst-case rent from Pennsylvania Avenue is $1700 for Boardwalk with four houses, but that would occur on a future turn.

I am now unsure whether mortgaging is allowed between turns. If it is not, the $42 bid simply reduces cash until my next turn. That is acceptable because the $726 buffer easily absorbs the loss. Even without immediate mortgage, the bid still blocks p4 from completing a green set.

p4 has $763 and is incrementing by $1. I will keep bidding $42 to stay below the $150 cap.

I now suspect p4 is also planning to mortgage North Carolina for $150. If so, the rational bid is up to $149. I will raise to $150 to secure the property and block p4 from completing a green set.

Blocking p4 from a second green is less valuable than it first appeared. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged by p1, so they cannot complete the set without trading.

If p4 wins and mortgages North Carolina, they still lose $150 net. The same arbitrage applies to both players.

The real question is whether to spend $150 now or let p4 spend it. p4 is in jail with light blues and unmortgaged railroads. That makes them more dangerous if they land on those spaces.

p1 is nearly broke with only $29 and heavily built dark blues. They might sell Pacific Avenue to p4 if p4 can pay. That would let p4 complete the green set later. This makes blocking p4 from North Carolina more valuable than it first appeared.
